extracted.intended_audience: agencies that administer civil monetary penalties, regulated entities (attorneys, compliance officers), and agency rulewriters
extracted.subtask_short: adjusting civil monetary penalties for inflation
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing and publishing inflation adjustments to civil monetary penalties (CMPs) under the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act and its 2015 improvements, including calculation method, timing, and required publications. This page is GSA's final rule applying those adjustments for PFCRA penalties and describing procedural/legal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to adjust CMPs for inflation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must make an initial inflationary adjustment for all applicable CMPs and make further adjustments at least once every year thereafter pursuant to the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act (as amended, including the 2015 Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As amended, the law requires each agency to make an initial inflationary adjustment for all applicable CMPs, and to make further adjustments at least once every year thereafter for these penalty amounts. The 2015 Act requires an initial “fix” and subsequent annual adjustments. (Page text explains purpose: to maintain remedial impact and promote compliance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing of adjustments (prospective application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any resulting increases in a CMP due to the calculated inflation adjustments shall apply only to violations which occur after the date the increase takes effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Debt Collection Improvement Act of 1996 stipulates increases apply only to violations occurring after the effective date, which this rule sets as 30 days after publication. (Original phrasing: 'any resulting increases ... shall apply only to violations which occur after the date the increase takes effect 30 days after the date of publication in the Federal Register.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Catch-up (initial) adjustment calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial or 'catch up' adjustment is based on the percent change between the Consumer Price Index for Urban Consumers (CPI-U) for the month of October for the year of the previous adjustment and the October 2015 CPI-U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2015 Act calls for a catch up adjustment 'based on the percent change between the Consumer Price Index for Urban Consumers (CPI-U) for the month of October for the year of the previous adjustment, and the October 2015 CPI-U.' This is the method used to compute the initial inflation-based increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent annual adjustment calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual adjustments are based on the percent change between the October CPI-U preceding the date of adjustment and the prior year's October CPI-U; if there is no increase, there is no adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For subsequent adjustments made in accordance with the 2015 Act, the amount of the adjustment is based on the percent increase between the CPI-U for the month of October preceding the date of the adjustment and the CPI-U for the October one year prior to the October immediately preceding the date of the adjustment. 'If there is no increase, there is no adjustment of civil penalties.' GSA will publish annual adjustments no later than January 15 each year (starting in 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for selecting maximum penalty (GSA specific, §105-70.003(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: For violations occurring on or after January 1, 2025, the maximum penalty assessed is the larger of: (1) the amount for the previous calendar year, or (2) an amount adjusted for inflation using the specified CPI-U percentage increase, then added to the previous-year amount and rounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text (paragraph (f)): 'the maximum penalty ... is the larger of: (1) The amount for the previous calendar year, or (2) An amount adjusted for inflation, calculated by multiplying the amount for the previous calendar year by the percentage by which the CPI-U for the month of October preceding the current calendar year exceeds the CPI-U for the month of October of the calendar year two years prior to the current calendar year, adding that amount to the amount for the previous calendar year, and rounding the total to the nearest hundred dollar increment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounding rule
rubrics_metrics.description: After calculating the inflation-adjusted total, round the total to the nearest hundred-dollar increment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As specified in the rule text: round the total to the nearest hundred dollar increment when computing the adjusted penalty amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: GSA will publish notice of the maximum penalty which may be assessed for calendar year 2026 and thereafter on an annual basis on or before January 15 of each calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (g) states: 'Notice of the maximum penalty ... for calendar year 2026 and thereafter will be published by GSA in the Federal Register on an annual basis on or before January 15 of each calendar year.' The rule also notes agencies generally must publish adjustments in the Federal Register no later than January 15 each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from notice-and-comment rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments required by the 2015 Act are expressly exempted from the notice and comment requirements of the Administrative Procedure Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvement Act of 2015 directs agencies to adjust CMPs 'notwithstanding section 553 of title 5, United States Code.' Therefore this final rule is issued without prior public notice or opportunity for public comment, with an effective date 30 days after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule (and the inflation adjustments) are effective 30 days after the date of publication in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple passages: effective 30 days after publication; the rule sets the effective date consistent with statutory direction that increases apply only to violations after the date the increase takes effect 30 days after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Orders / OMB review determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency must consider E.O. 12866 and E.O. 13563 and whether the rule is a 'significant regulatory action' requiring OMB review; OMB determined this GSA rule 'does not meet the criteria for a significant regulatory action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule notes E.O.s 12866 and 13563 direct agencies to assess costs/benefits. 'The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) has reviewed this final rule ... and has determined that it does not meet the criteria for a significant regulatory action.' This informs whether additional review or analyses are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a rule may take effect, the agency must submit a rule report (including a copy of the rule) to both Houses of Congress and the Comptroller General as required by the CRA; GSA will submit such a report and has determined the rule is not a 'major rule.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'GSA will submit a report containing this rule and other required information to the U.S. Senate, the U.S. House of Representatives, and the Comptroller General of the United States.' The agency and OMB determined the rule is not a major rule under 5 U.S.C. 804(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: RFA requires a regulatory flexibility analysis unless the agency certifies no significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; RFA does not apply here because the agency is not required to publish a proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule explains: 'The RFA applies only to rules for which an agency is required to first publish a proposed rule ... As explained above, GSA is not required to first publish a proposed rule here. Thus, the RFA does not apply to this final rule.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule imposes no new reporting or recordkeeping requirements that would necessitate OMB clearance under the PRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text states explicitly: 'This final rule imposes no new reporting or recordkeeping requirements necessitating clearance by OMB.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of penalty and PFCRA context
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program Fraud Civil Remedies Act (PFCRA) imposes a civil monetary penalty and an assessment against any person who, with knowledge or reason to know, makes, submits, or presents a false, fictitious, or fraudulent claim or statement to the Government; GSA's regulation sets the maximum penalty amount for such violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule describes PFCRA background and gives the prior maximum penalty amount ($13,400) and the adjusted amount ($13,700) based on the CPI-based annual adjustment calculation described in the rule.
